findings: UpdateTaskParams is a non_exhaustive camelCase request-params struct with exactly the public fields meta: Option<RequestMetaObject>, task_id: String, and input_responses: InputResponses. UpdateTaskParams::new(task_id, input_responses) sets meta=None.

On the standard ServerHandler Service<RoleServer> dispatch path, UpdateTaskRequest is capability-gated before the custom update_task handler is invoked. If the server does not advertise Tasks, the dispatcher returns Method not found; if the client did not declare Tasks, it returns Missing Required Client Capability. Only after that gate does it call self.update_task(request.params, context) and map Ok(()) to the stock task acknowledgement.

Stock TaskManager::update_task first sweeps expiry, resolves the task by id, returns unknown_task(task_id) when absent, consumes supplied inputResponses by removing only matching pending-input keys and sending their values, ignores unknown/already-answered/superseded keys, touches last_updated_at, recomputes current status, and returns Ok(()).

unknown_task(task_id) is ErrorData::invalid_params(format!("unknown task: {task_id}"), None). The exact source test states nonexistent taskId is INVALID_PARAMS for tasks/get and SHOULD be INVALID_PARAMS for update/cancel.

No Tasks-specific post-handler error conversion changes update_task errors. The only post-dispatch remap in this handler is RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND to INVALID_PARAMS for 2026-07-28+ peers, which is unrelated to TaskManager::unknown_task because that helper already emits INVALID_PARAMS.

Therefore revision 65's error-map conclusion survives exact release verification: unknown/nonexistent taskId maps directly to INVALID_PARAMS; an application-owned stale-generation or intent-conflict check has no stock task-specific error code and may use INVALID_PARAMS as a non-invented request-parameter rejection, but that extension mapping remains application policy rather than an rmcp guarantee.

compile_risk_reduced_adapter_sketch.shape: Implement ServerHandler::update_task with the exact released signature update_task(&self, request: UpdateTaskParams, context: RequestContext<RoleServer>) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), McpError>> + MaybeSendFuture + '_. Route request.task_id plus request.input_responses into the application-owned persistent task store. Return Ok(()) on accepted delivery; map UnknownTask to McpError::invalid_params. If the persistent protocol adds stale-generation/intent checks, reject them before mutation and map them consistently as application-level INVALID_PARAMS unless a separately source-qualified extension contract defines another code.
do_not_duplicate: Do not manufacture TaskAckResult inside update_task; standard Service dispatch maps Result<(), McpError> to ServerResult::task_ack.

Do not duplicate the stock Tasks capability gate inside update_task when all remote requests enter through the standard ServerHandler Service dispatch; direct internal method calls would bypass that dispatcher gate and must not be treated as equivalent remote-policy execution.
Do not use stock TaskManager as the persistent backend; its in-memory TaskContext/HashMap lifetime boundary remains unresolved for restart durability.

tested_scope.scope_limit: This slice verifies released wire fields, standard dispatcher capability gating, stock update control flow/error mapping, and a compile-risk-reduced adapter shape only. It does not prove the custom persistent store, restart redriver, or effect fencing.

residual_dependency_detail: A persistent application-owned task store/redriver plus external-effect idempotency or fencing remains an unresolved child; this slice does not convert that architecture into a Phase-1 pass.
conflict_check: Own role-local state plus public release source only; no O, other-worker, downstream, legacy, shared-ledger, other-role receipt/config semantics were consumed.
